text:
maya_pm: Hey team — I dropped a first-pass PRD for the Console telemetry work into the doc: https://go.redwood/prd/console-telemetry-v1 :link: Can we confirm must-have acceptance criteria and decide what to cut for MVP? Need decisions by EOD tomorrow so eng can slot sprint 12.
jon_engineer: skimmed. Big 👍 on the tiers approach but we should be explicit about query latency budget for the UI. Also need to call out sampling levels for traces.
sam_sre: agree we need budgets. Proposal: console query p50 < 50ms, p95 < 200ms under normal load (current dashboard load). Also retention tiering can't blow up storage — estimate 2.4x at 90d vs 30d unless we add rollup/aggregation.
rita_ux: UX asks: what search flows do we keep? MVP: timeline + free-text + trace link. Can we drop advanced histogram faceting to phase 2? :thinking_face:
maya_pm: thinking MVP = core dashboards (latency, errors, cost), trace detail with sampled spans, retention tiers (30d default / 90d paid). Drop per-route retention and deep analytics for phase 2.
leo_qa: need clear acceptance test list. Adding common edge cases: missing trace_id propagation, truncated spans, partial ingestion windows. I'll add tests.
nina_prodops: rollout plan should include opt-in beta orgs, canary at 1% of tenant-traffic, then 10%, 50%. Must include rollback criteria (error spike, 2xx->5xx >1.5x baseline).
jon_engineer: quick technical note: we'll implement retention using rollup + partitioned compact storage. For traces we sample 10% global by default, 100% for critical services tag. We should include a config snippet:

```
telemetry.retention:
  default_days: 30
  paid_tiers: [90, 365]
trace.sampling:
  default: 0.10
  overrides:
    service: {payment-gateway: 1.0}
```

sam_sre: sampling override for critical services ok but add guard to prevent 100% across many services (cost spike).
maya_pm: proposed acceptance criteria (draft) — please comment inline. I'll paste here to capture on thread:

```
Acceptance criteria v0 (MVP):
1) Dashboards: latency, error-rate, token-cost per-route present and queryable; default time window choices 1h/24h/7d/30d.
2) Retention: default 30d, paid tiers 90d and 365d; data older than tier must be queryable via rollups; export path for long-term archive.
3) Tracing: sampled traces surfaced in timeline; trace link from span to full trace; 10% default sampling with config override for tagged services.
4) Performance: console queries meet p95 < 200ms and p50 < 50ms under baseline traffic.
5) Reliability: no user-visible errors introduced by rollout; rollback if error rate or increase in 5xxs exceeds threshold.
6) Migration: existing telemetry mapped to new schema without data loss for last 30d.
```

rita_ux: UI acceptance: query state preserved when navigating, filter chips, and breadcrumbs. Also need empty-state copy for low-data orgs. I'll add screenshots in the doc.
leo_qa: edge cases to add to ACs: partial index writes (simulate node failure), delayed ingestion windows causing backfills, and queries returning partial aggregates. Also test RBAC: org-level retention overrides shouldn't leak to other orgs.
jon_engineer: one more deferral: per-route token-cost breakdown is heavy — for MVP we can show per-model and per-service rollups; postpone per-route until we have efficient per-route summarization.
maya_pm: sounds sensible. So decision: cut per-route token-cost in MVP, keep per-model and service-level. Capture decision in PRD now.
telemetry-bot: scheduled export job created: telemetry/export/2024-04-01 -> s3://redwood-telemetry-archive (info)
sam_sre: rollout gating checklist we need in PRD: a) canary latency within budget b) no increase in error-rate c) storage growth within forecast +/-20% d) query success rate > 99%.
nina_prodops: add operational runbook steps and cost alert thresholds. Recommend an initial alert for storage growth >10% week-over-week for 2 weeks.
maya_pm: thanks — I'm going to update the doc with these ACs and the decision to trim scope. If anyone has an objection to the trimmed MVP, raise it now, otherwise I'll mark as decided and we can move to sprint planning.
jon_engineer: no objection from eng side, will prepare implementation estimate after doc update.
rita_ux: no objection from design.
leo_qa: QA aligned.
sam_sre: SRE aligned, but require post-canary monitoring dashboard and automated rollback hook.
maya_pm: great — closing loop. I'll update PRD and ping for final review once changes are in. :thumbsup:
